method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)' (published June 2019). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. claims.claim: **Kaposi sarcoma is a multicentric tumour of lymphatic-endothelial cells infected with HHV-8.** Its four subtypes are classic, endemic (sub-Saharan Africa), epidemic (HIV) and iatrogenic (immunosuppression, especially transplant); the degree of immunosuppression drives onset and progression.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lesions are purple, red-blue or brown macules, plaques or nodules** that can bleed, ulcerate or become warty; lymphoedema is common and may appear first.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classic KS is usually indolent; HIV-related and post-transplant KS can be extensive and life-threatening.**
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In HIV, KS remains the second most common cancer in Western countries.** Low CD4 is the main risk factor, but risk stays above the general population even with normal CD4 and suppressed viral load.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After organ transplant, KS risk is 50- to 500-fold higher,** peaking in the first 2 years; median onset is 13 months after transplant.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Biopsy is mandatory.** Staining for the HHV-8 LANA protein is the best way to tell KS from its mimics.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HHV-8 viral load in blood is not usable** to monitor KS or predict it in transplant recipients.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Only AIDS-related KS has a validated staging system (ACTG: tumour, immune, systemic symptoms);** since antiretroviral therapy, the tumour and symptom components carry the prognosis. Otherwise, sort patients into localised non-aggressive, locally aggressive or disseminated disease.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No randomised trial compares the local options.**
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Radiotherapy is among the most effective treatments for localised KS** (response 47% to 99%). Avoid more than 3 Gy per fraction and concurrent systemic therapy to limit late effects.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Surgery recurs often;** keep it for a few small, well-defined superficial lesions.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CO2 laser or superficial cryotherapy can work for a while on superficial lesions;** warn about lasting hypopigmentation.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intralesional chemotherapy** (vinblastine, response about 70%) and **electrochemotherapy** (bleomycin with electroporation) are effective local options.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Topical options:** imiquimod helped about half of 17 patients with classic or endemic KS (local itch and redness in 53%); alitretinoin 0.1% gel gave a 37% response in HIV-related KS on antiretrovirals.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The aim is control, symptom relief and quality of life, not cure.** The preferred first-line drugs are paclitaxel and pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD).
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **PLD 20 mg/m² every 3 weeks:** response 76% in HIV-related KS on antiretrovirals and higher in classic KS; responses last a median of about 5 months (HIV) and 25 months (classic). Grade IV neutropenia and hand–foot syndrome each occur in about 5%.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Paclitaxel 100 mg/m² every 2 weeks** gives about 60% response in HIV-related KS. Against PLD in a randomised trial, progression-free survival was similar (17.5 vs 12.2 months) but toxicity was greater, so it is second line in HIV-related KS.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For non-AIDS KS, the preferred paclitaxel schedule is 80 mg/m² weekly,** continuously or 3 weeks on and 1 off.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vinblastine, oral etoposide and bleomycin are alternatives,** not first-line choices.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HIV-related KS: start antiretroviral therapy first;** most lesions regress. Add chemotherapy for poor-prognosis (T1) or rapidly progressive disease, and to prevent or treat IRIS.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With antiretrovirals, liposomal anthracyclines are first line and taxanes second.** The herpesvirus (KSHV) cannot be cleared and KS can recur; if long-term cytotoxics are not tolerated, pomalidomide or lenalidomide may be discussed.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Post-transplant KS: reduce immunosuppression to the lowest level and switch to an mTOR inhibitor such as sirolimus** while protecting the graft; add systemic therapy for extensive or life-threatening disease. Avoid interferon alfa (rejection risk).
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classic/endemic KS needs systemic treatment when aggressive** (nodal or visceral disease, severe oedema, complications or rapid spread): usually liposomal anthracycline, less often weekly taxane. Low-dose interferon alfa is an option under 70 with normal cardiac function.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Life-threatening disease (extensive HIV-KS, IRIS, severe post-transplant KS): review at least monthly and image at least every 3 months until stable.** Indolent classic KS can be seen every six months to a year, mainly clinically. Repeat biopsy only for atypical course or to confirm nodal or visceral spread.
claims.locator: European Dermatology Forum, European Association of Dermato-Oncology and EORTC (Lebbé C, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2019;114:117–127, 'Diagnosis and treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline (EDF/EADO/EORTC)', published June 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2018.12.036, retrieved 2026-09-23
